description: Plays one MPX part on a physically modelled guitar: nylon-string, steel-string or electric. Each string is a digital waveguide, picked, hammered, slid, palm-muted, bent or touched for harmonics as the part's notes specify. The strings sound through an acoustic body, or an electric pickup and amplifier, in stereo.

params.name: Pick position
params.text: Where the strings are picked, as a distance from the bridge: 2% to 50% of the string length, 15% by default. Nearer the bridge gives a thinner, brighter sound; nearer the middle, a rounder, softer one. Partials with a node at the picking point are not sounded.

params.name: Brightness
params.text: Hardness of the pick. Fully counter-clockwise, a fingertip: the attack is rounded and partials above about 200 Hz are reduced. At two thirds, a hard plectrum, with a click as it leaves the string. Above two thirds the click is louder, up to three times a plectrum's.

params.name: Sustain
params.text: Ring time of the open low E string: the time its fundamental takes to fall 60 dB, 0.5 s to 20 s, 5 s by default. Higher notes ring for less time as set by Taper, and fretted notes as set by Fret damping. Shorter settings also lose upper partials faster, so they sound duller.

params.name: Body
params.text: Nylon and Steel-string: how much of the body's sound is heard, from the bare strings fully counter-clockwise to a full body at two thirds. That includes the air resonance near 100 Hz, the top plate's resonances above it, and the high-frequency roll-off. Above two thirds the resonances are stronger than a real body's. Electric: the pickup position, from the bridge, thinner and brighter, to the neck, rounder and warmer.

params.name: Guitar
params.text: Selects the guitar. Nylon: a classical guitar with nylon strings, played with the fingertip, whose high partials decay quickly. Steel-string: an acoustic with steel strings, brighter and stiffer. Electric: steel strings through a magnetic pickup and an amplifier, with Tone, Drive, Bass, Middle and Treble controls added to the panel.

params.name: Tone
params.text: Electric only: two low-pass filter stages before the amplifier. Fully clockwise, no filtering; fully counter-clockwise, frequencies above 300 Hz are rolled off.

params.name: Drive
params.text: Electric only: amplifier drive, from 1 to 18. Fully counter-clockwise, single notes are clean and loud chords begin to distort; fully clockwise, everything is heavily distorted.

params.name: Sympathy
params.text: How much the unplayed strings resonate with the played ones, each at its open pitch, through the bridge. Fully counter-clockwise, none; at one third, the default, the level of a typical acoustic guitar; fully clockwise, three times that.

params.name: Finger noise
params.text: Level of the squeak of a finger sliding along a wound string, in slides into, out of and between notes. Fully counter-clockwise, none; fully clockwise, louder than a real player's. Bends make no squeak.

params.name: Stiffness
params.text: String stiffness: the stiffer the string, the further its upper partials are tuned sharp of exact multiples of the fundamental. Fully clockwise, the eighth partial is 9 cents sharp on every string, more than any real string. Nylon strings get one sixth of the setting.

params.name: Strum speed
params.text: Time a strummed chord takes to cross the strings, 0 to 45 ms, 18 ms by default. At 0, all the strings sound together.

params.name: Taper
params.text: How much shorter high notes ring than low ones. Fully counter-clockwise, every note rings as long as Sustain sets. Otherwise, each octave above the open low E rings for a fraction of the time of the octave below: 0.66 at one third, the default, and 0.29 fully clockwise.

params.name: Fret damping
params.text: How much a fretting finger shortens and dulls a note compared with the open string. Fully counter-clockwise, fretted and open notes ring the same; at one third, the default, a fretted note rings three quarters as long; fully clockwise, a quarter as long and much duller.

params.name: Humanise
params.text: Random variation in each note's timing, level and length, different in each copy of the module. Fully counter-clockwise, none; at one third, the default, that of a typical player; fully clockwise, three times that, with notes spread over about 18 ms, as many early as late around a delay of 9 ms.

params.name: Bass
params.text: Electric only: amplifier low shelf below about 100 Hz, -18 dB to +18 dB.

params.name: Middle
params.text: Electric only: amplifier mid band around 500 Hz, -18 dB to +18 dB.

params.name: Treble
params.text: Electric only: amplifier high shelf above about 3 kHz, -18 dB to +18 dB.

inputs.name: MPX note
inputs.text: The part to play, from mpxScore or any other MPX source, including how each note is played. The instrument named on the cable sets the strings' tuning and capo, and is shown below the guitar selector.

outputs.name: Left
outputs.text: The left and right channels of the stereo audio. A single note at a moderate dynamic peaks at about 2 V.

outputs.name: Right
outputs.text: The left and right channels of the stereo audio. A single note at a moderate dynamic peaks at about 2 V.

lights.name: Level
lights.text: Flashes green when a note is struck. Orange when the output exceeds 7.07 V, 3 dB below clipping; red when it reaches 10 V, where Rack's audio interface clips. Red is held for 1 s and orange for 0.3 s.

notes: Timing, dynamics, strums, bends and articulations are worked out from the part by the same performance rules as mpxGuitarist. The rules are read from DreamerMPX/perform.txt in the Rack user folder when the module starts, and again with Read the performance rules again in the right-click menu.
A knob change takes effect on each string the next time it is picked.

Choosing Electric widens the module with a column of five more controls: Tone, Drive, Bass, Middle and Treble. Choosing Nylon or Steel-string narrows it again. Modules to the right are pushed along as it widens, and stay where they are as it narrows.
